Mimosa Launches New Platinum Alloy Product to Bolster Zimbabwe’s Mining Sector

Mimosa, a prominent player in Zimbabwe’s metals and mining industry, has announced the launch of a new platinum alloy product, marking a significant step for the sector. The unveiling event took place at the company’s Zvishavane operations on Thursday, drawing attendance from industry officials, local leaders, and representatives from the Chamber of Mines.

The new alloy, dubbed “MimAlloy-P,” is designed to meet growing demand for durable and versatile materials in the global manufacturing and automotive markets. According to company officials, the product combines high-grade platinum with select base metals to enhance corrosion resistance and thermal stability.

“MimAlloy-P is the result of years of research and development here in Zimbabwe,” said Tawanda Moyo, Mimosa’s Technical Director. “We are proud to offer a product that not only meets international standards but also showcases local innovation and expertise.”

Analysts say the launch positions Zimbabwe to capture more value from its platinum resources and could provide a boost to export earnings. “This is a positive development for the industry, showing how local beneficiation can create jobs and drive economic growth,” commented Tendai Gwindi, an independent mining analyst based in Harare.

The Zimbabwe Miners’ Association also welcomed the move. “We applaud Mimosa for setting a benchmark in value addition,” said association secretary, Rudo Dube. “Such initiatives support the government’s vision of transforming mining into a US$12 billion industry by 2025.”

Production of MimAlloy-P will commence immediately, with initial shipments expected to reach regional and international markets by the end of the third quarter. The company has indicated plans to further expand its product range in the coming year.
